analysis.title: Enphase Energy Inc. (ENPH): An update on the SST roadmap; GaN technology in focus; remain Buy
key_insights: On 10/26, ENPH and Infineon announced the world's first 900 V monolithic GaN bidirectional switch (BDS) for ENPH's solid-state transformer (SST) power modules for AI data centers. GS views it as a technology milestone.

ENPH already uses 650 V GaN BDS devices in its IQ9 microinverters. The expanded work with Infineon's CoolGaN bidirectional switch portfolio extends GaN into higher-voltage applications. ENPH also published a technical white paper on its GaN BDS architecture.

A monolithic GaN BDS switches in both directions in a single device, where conventional bidirectional switches need two back-to-back transistors. ENPH estimates a 4x die-area advantage and up to a 4x cost advantage versus back-to-back GaN configurations.

ENPH estimates about a 10x die-area and 20x gate-charge advantage versus equivalent back-to-back silicon MOSFETs. Lower gate charge allows higher switching frequencies, which means smaller magnetic and filtering components and a smaller system.

ENPH believes GaN BDS can be more cost-effective than comparable silicon solutions despite GaN's higher underlying semiconductor cost. It cites third-party research that GaN HEMTs have about 10x greater single-event burnout robustness than comparable SiC MOSFETs and about 60x greater than silicon MOSFETs.

The 900 V device is a step up from the 650 V class of commercially available GaN BDS devices. Research institutions have shown monolithic GaN BDS at higher voltages, including 1.2 kV-class devices. ENPH believes 900 V is the practical economic limit of the existing GaN-on-silicon process, and higher voltages would need alternative insulating substrates.
ENPH is working with semiconductor partners toward potential 1.2 kV-class GaN BDS devices. GS reads 900 V as a commercial milestone rather than the technological endpoint for GaN.

GS says the 900 V BDS pushes GaN into applications historically served by SiC while keeping high-frequency switching, efficiency and power density. It expands the modular architecture's reach to megawatt-scale uses, including higher-voltage utility feeds and a pathway toward future 1,500 VDC data center architectures.
GS says the announcement validates ENPH's strategy of applying its GaN power-conversion experience from microinverters to the much larger power needs of AI data centers.

Roadmap: a full ~4.2 MW, 13.8 kV SST system demonstration at ENPH test facilities in late November 2026, shipment to a national laboratory for validation in 1Q27, and demo/test module production at the automated Arlington, Texas plant. Customer pilots are scheduled for 1H27, initial commercial deployments as early as 4Q27, and a more meaningful AI data center revenue ramp in 2028.
GS keeps its Buy rating with a 12-month price target of $47 against a $31.60 price (23 Oct 2026 close), 48.7% upside. The target uses a 20x P/E on Q5-Q8 EPS plus about $7 of net cash per share.

market_movers.rationale: GS sees the 900 V GaN BDS as validating ENPH's move from microinverters into SSTs for AI data centers. The target is 20x Q5-Q8 EPS plus about $7 net cash per share.

earnings_insights: GS estimates (not reported results): ENPH EPS $2.05 for 12/26E, $2.08 for 12/27E and $2.57 for 12/28E, versus $2.97 actual for 12/25.
GS quarterly EPS: $0.46 for 6/26 and estimates of $0.54 for 9/26E, $0.59 for 12/26E and $0.40 for 3/27E.
GS revenue estimates: $1,178.7mn for 12/26E, $1,094.8mn for 12/27E and $1,248.5mn for 12/28E, versus $1,473.0mn for 12/25.
risk_factors: Changes in the competitive and technology landscape
Abnormal inventory builds across the channel
geopolitical: US-China tariffs are listed among the key risks to ENPH.
